expectedRealization.rationale: Power-equipment backlog and capacity conversion are multi-quarter mechanisms; a fresh company-selection edge should be visible through order quality, margins and earnings conversion rather than a short price reaction.

changeHypothesis.summary: GE Vernova and ABB independently showed a genuine further acceleration in global electrification/data-center orders. The A-share opportunity remained real, but the frozen Q1 company evidence did not identify a newly differentiated winner: 思源电气 had strong revenue/order context but slower reported profit growth, while 伊戈尔 had faster profit growth from a smaller base but weaker revenue growth and sharply negative operating cash flow.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: Two independent first-party global suppliers reported large order/backlog acceleration, including data-center electrical equipment.
disconfirmingEvidence: The theme had already been strong since 2025, increasing expectation saturation.
思源 Q1 reported profit growth well below revenue growth.
伊戈尔 Q1 operating cash flow deteriorated sharply and revenue growth was only 17.7%.

selectionComparison.rationale: The industry event is high priority, but neither frozen A-share candidate showed a sufficiently clean new price-relative company reset to justify selection.

expectations.marketExpectationAtCutoff: The global power-equipment shortage/backlog narrative was already well established. 思源's Q1 revenue was strong but profit conversion was less impressive; 伊戈尔 showed profit acceleration but weaker top-line/cash conversion.
expectations.thesisExpectation: The global order cycle can remain structurally strong, but the system should wait for a fresh company-specific order/margin reset before selecting.
expectations.measurableGap: Opportunity-level acceleration is verified; stock-level expectation gap is not.
